svg.title: When information has time to pay: the Horizon task and two qualitative exploration model properties
svg.desc: Panel A shows the Horizon task. Two alternative sample-history cards, equal information (two forced samples from each of two machines, L and R) and unequal information (three from L, one from R, which is tagged as less sampled), are grouped as four forced samples. An arrow labeled Then leads to two alternative free-choice timelines: one free choice, or six free choices. Each free-choice box shows a pair of machines to choose between. The first box of each timeline has the same dark ring, labeled first free choice; boxes two to six of the long timeline are bracketed as five later choices. A note states that each sampling condition occurs at both horizons. Panels B and C each carry the label Schematic, not data, which stays with separate panel crops. Left and right assignments in panel A are illustrative. The choice curves use illustrative parameters, not estimates for either horizon. Panel B, bias toward information: probability of choosing the less-sampled option against the estimated reward difference (less-sampled minus more-sampled). Two parallel rising curves; the larger-information-bonus curve (ochre, dashed) is shifted left of the smaller-bonus curve (blue, solid) and is higher at zero difference. Note: longer horizon, larger bonus. Panel C, looser reward-guided choice: probability of choosing the right option against the estimated reward difference (right minus left). Two rising curves centered at zero; the more-decision-noise curve (ochre, dashed) is flatter than the less-decision-noise curve (blue, solid), higher on the negative side and lower on the positive side, but still rising. Note: longer horizon, more noise.

g.text: Each sampling condition occurs at both horizons
